item.title: On the Unrolling of the Real Line
item.description: §01 § I. The Axioms of Peano peano.1889 N N ow, the natural numbers arise not from experience but from the form of thought itself. Peano, following Dedekind's Was sind und was sollen die Zahlen?, distilled arithmetic to five propositions — each as spare and hard as flint — from which the entire edifice of number shall be raised stone by stone. Let ℕ denote the set in question, 0 its least element, and S the successor function: the engine of increment, the pulse of counting.
